summary: We walked 13 paths on your Mac. 13 came back clear. You're okay tonight.
leader_line: Breathe. Nothing here needs you tonight.

clear_checks.name: Launch ghosts
clear_checks.looked_at: Startup lists (LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, login items) that point at apps or files that are missing
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Apps that still launch but behave badly, or kernel-level malware
clear_checks.why_matters: Broken launch items slow login and are a common place scareware hides after you delete the main app

clear_checks.name: Adware markers
clear_checks.detail: No known scareware patterns in common spots.
clear_checks.looked_at: Known adware file names, folders, and browser-extension patterns left on disk
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Brand-new malware with no known signature, or threats only in memory
clear_checks.why_matters: Fake virus popups often leave named leftovers · finding them explains odd browser behavior

clear_checks.name: Hosts file
clear_checks.looked_at: Your Mac's hosts file for unexpected redirects to sketchy domains
clear_checks.does_not_cover: DNS changes made only on your router or phone, or VPN-only routing
clear_checks.why_matters: Scareware sometimes edits hosts to lock you onto their "support" pages

clear_checks.name: DNS resolvers
clear_checks.looked_at: Which DNS servers your Mac is set to use (Wi‑Fi and Ethernet)
clear_checks.does_not_cover: DNS on other devices, or encrypted DNS inside a browser only
clear_checks.why_matters: Fake cleaners often switch DNS so they can intercept or nag you on every site

clear_checks.name: System proxy
clear_checks.looked_at: System-wide web proxy settings that could funnel traffic through a stranger
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Browser-only extensions, or corporate proxies your IT installed on purpose
clear_checks.why_matters: Unexpected proxies are a classic persistence trick after scare popups

clear_checks.name: Gatekeeper
clear_checks.looked_at: Whether macOS Gatekeeper and quarantine protections are turned on as expected
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Whether every app you run is trustworthy · only whether core guards are enabled
clear_checks.why_matters: Disabled Gatekeeper makes it easier to run downloaded scareware installers

clear_checks.name: Security software
clear_checks.looked_at: Whether known security tools (Malwarebytes, etc.) are installed and responding
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Full scans, license status, or whether those tools found anything today
clear_checks.why_matters: Knowing what protection you already have avoids duplicate panic subscriptions

clear_checks.name: Firefox profile
clear_checks.looked_at: Firefox profiles for suspicious extensions, search hijacks, and odd home pages
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Safari or Chrome, or activity inside private windows we cannot see
clear_checks.why_matters: After a bad link, browsers are often the first place redirects and spam extensions land

clear_checks.name: Safari profile
clear_checks.looked_at: Safari extensions and homepage/search settings for obvious hijacks
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Firefox or Chrome, or iCloud-synced settings on other devices
clear_checks.why_matters: Safari is the default browser · scare pages often target it first on Mac

clear_checks.name: Chrome profile
clear_checks.looked_at: Chrome profiles for suspicious extensions, policies, and search overrides
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Other browsers, or Chrome on a different user account
clear_checks.why_matters: Extension spam after a scare popup usually shows up as odd Chrome behavior

clear_checks.name: Login items
clear_checks.detail: Login items match what you'd expect.
clear_checks.looked_at: Items set to open automatically when you log in (System Settings list)
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Background services that do not appear in Login Items, or iCloud-only apps
clear_checks.why_matters: Mystery login items are a common "why is my Mac slow?" clue after scareware

clear_checks.name: Recent installs
clear_checks.detail: No surprise installers in the last week.
clear_checks.looked_at: Apps and packages installed in roughly the last seven days
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Installs older than a week, or drag-and-drop apps with no installer record
clear_checks.why_matters: The thing you installed right after the popup is often the actual trouble

clear_checks.name: Configuration profiles
clear_checks.looked_at: Configuration and MDM profiles that can lock settings or install remote management
clear_checks.does_not_cover: Profiles your employer installed on a work Mac you already expect
clear_checks.why_matters: Unexpected profiles can mean someone else controls settings on your personal Mac

does_not_check: Real-time malware scanning, removal, or quarantine of active threats
Whether someone else is reading your email, iCloud, or bank accounts right now
Network traffic, keystrokes, or screen capture while you use the Mac
Windows, Linux, iPhone, or iPad (Macintosh only today)
Guaranteed proof that nothing bad will ever happen later
scope_lead: A clear scout is honest about its lane. Passing these checks means we did not see common scareware leftovers in the places we read · not that your Mac is invulnerable forever.
